title: Get-Home Bag
description: Use this list to pack a small bag for work or your car so you can get home on foot, or wait safely, for 24-48 hours.

items.text: Broken-in walking shoes or boots and two pairs of good socks - dress shoes stop most people walking home
At least 1 liter (1 quart) of water in a bottle that will not burst if frozen, plus a small filter or purification tablets
A few days of any daily prescription medicine and a written medicine list
Headlamp with spare batteries so your hands stay free
Small power bank and phone cable
Paper map of the area between work and home with 2-3 routes marked, avoiding bridges, tunnels, and low ground
Written phone numbers and an out-of-area contact; agree on who texts whom
Rain jacket or poncho, warm layer, hat, and gloves for your worst season
About 2,000 calories of no-cook food: energy bars, nuts, jerky
Small first aid kit with gloves and blister care (moleskin or blister bandages)
Compact emergency blanket or bivy
Whistle
N95 mask for dust or smoke
Cash in small bills and a copy of your ID
Multi-tool (if allowed at your workplace), a little duct tape, and 25-50 feet (8-15 m) of cord
Work gloves, small lighter, hand sanitizer, and a bandana
Sun protection in hot places: cap and sunscreen
Small compass, if you know how to use it
Plan with family ahead of time who picks up children from school and where you will meet
Know when to stay put: do not walk into a storm, extreme heat, smoke, or floodwater if you can shelter safely
Use a plain day pack that looks like a normal work or school bag
Swap food, water, and seasonal clothing every 6 months; use lithium batteries and keep power banks out of a hot car in summer
